content: 1. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inhibiting the metabolism of CYP3A4 enzymes in the liver and intestines. Close monitoring is required, as this interaction may increase the risk of adverse reactions associated with CYP3A4 substrates, particularly within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir. 2. Lesinurad decreases the effectiveness of norethindrone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives should not be relied upon as the sole method of contraception during lesinurad therapy. Additional non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 3. Letermovir increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 4. Levoketoconazole increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is uncertain, but close monitoring is recommended. 5. Lopinavir increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 6. Lorlatinib decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered, and hormonal contraceptive dosages may need adjustment. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended during and after lorlatinib therapy. 7. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable during coadministration. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are advised, and the risk of menstrual-related adverse effects may increase. 8. Maraviroc levels may increase when coadministered with norethindrone due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and close monitoring are required to avoid potential toxicity. 9. Mavacamten decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative contraceptive methods unaffected by CYP450 induction, such as intrauterine systems or condoms, are recommended during and for four months after mavacamten therapy. 10. Metformin's effects may be reduced by norethindrone due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 11. Mifepristone increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism but also decreases its effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Backup contraceptive methods are recommended, and close monitoring is required. 12. Mitotane decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration, and non-hormonal methods are advised. Menstrual-related adverse effects may increase. 13. Nafcillin decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended during therapy. 14. Nelfinavir increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 15. Nemolizumab decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism through cytokine suppression. Dosage adjustments of CYP substrates may be necessary, and close monitoring is required. 16. Phenobarbital decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration, and non-hormonal methods are advised. Menstrual-related adverse effects may increase. 17. Phenytoin decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration, and non-hormonal methods are advised. Menstrual-related adverse effects may increase. 18. Primidone decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration, and non-hormonal methods are advised. Menstrual-related adverse effects may increase. 19. Ribociclib increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is uncertain, but close monitoring is recommended. 20. Rifabutin decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration, and non-hormonal methods are advised. Menstrual-related adverse effects may increase. 21. Rifampin decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration, and non-hormonal methods are advised. Menstrual-related adverse effects may increase. 22. Rifapentine decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration, and non-hormonal methods are advised. Menstrual-related adverse effects may increase. 23. Ritonavir increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 24. Rucaparib increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dosage adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary, and close monitoring is required. 25. Rufinamide decreases norethindrone levels by weakly inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required, as rufinamide may reduce the effectiveness of CYP3A4 substrates. 26. Siltuximab may restore CYP450 enzymatic activity by inhibiting IL-6, potentially altering the metabolism of CYP substrates. Caution and close monitoring are advised when coadministered with narrow therapeutic index drugs. 27. Stiripentol inhibits and induces CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially altering the effects of coadministered CYP3A4 substrates. Dosage adjustments may be necessary, and close monitoring is required. 28. Sugammadex decreases norethindrone effects by competing for receptor binding. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended for seven days after sugammadex administration. 29. Tazemetostat decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 30. Tecovirimat decreases norethindrone levels by weakly inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required to ensure the effectiveness of CYP3A4 substrates. 31. Tesamorelin decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative contraceptive methods are recommended. 32. Tipranavir increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 33. Topiramate decreases norethindrone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable during coadministration, and non-hormonal methods are advised. Menstrual-related adverse effects may increase. 34. Tucatinib increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with CYP3A substrates unless necessary, and reduce substrate doses if unavoidable. 35. Voriconazole increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 36. Common adverse effects of norethindrone include edema, weakness, anorexia, amenorrhea, breakthrough bleeding, changes in menstrual flow, spotting, deep vein thrombosis, thrombophlebitis, depression, dizziness, headache, nervousness, somnolence, breast tenderness, galactorrhea, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, weight changes, cholestatic jaundice, and gastrointestinal disorders. 37. Rare but serious adverse effects include hepatic adenomas, focal nodular hyperplasia, and fatal intra-abdominal hemorrhage. Irregular menstrual bleeding is common with progestin-only contraceptives, and ectopic pregnancy should be considered in patients with lower abdominal pain. 38. Discontinue norethindrone if jaundice, severe migraines, significant blood pressure increases, or signs of thromboembolic complications occur.
